newsitem.title: BELGIUM: No quick end to British beef ban - EU commissioner.
newsitem.headline: No quick end to British beef ban - EU commissioner.

text.p: European Union Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler ruled out on Monday any speedy end to a worldwide ban on British beef exports if Britain announces plans to cull an extra 100,000 cattle at risk from mad cow disease.
The British government confirmed in London that Agriculture Minister Douglas Hogg would make a statement to parliament on Monday on mad cow disease and the export ban on British beef.
"I think we need to move forward step by step as agreed," Fischler told a news conference.
Fischler said that Britain agreed at an EU summit in Florence in June to pre-conditions, including the selective cull, for lifting the ban.
If the conditions have been fulfilled, then the next step would be for Britain to submit a working document as to how the ban should be gradually lifted, he said.
"I have not been informed that the U.K. is going to make a proposal today. We have not received a copy," he added.
The working document would then be examined by various EU scientific committees before being sent for a vote by the EU's Standing Veterinary Committee of senior national officials.
The EU's executive Commission would then take a final decision.
"I don't see any reason why we should now depart from what was agreed upon," he said.

The EU imposed a ban on British beef exports in March after the British government disclosed that the disease, known medically as Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE), could spread to people who ate infected beef.
But Britain said in September it was suspending the scheme after fresh scientific evidence suggested that BSE would be eradicated by the year 2001 under existing measures.
Hogg is due to report to EU farm ministers on Tuesday on progress in eradicating mad cow disease, which has ravaged British herds over the past 10 years.
